proof_scope: VS Code selected-range reveal: the debugger bridge opens a file in the trusted workspace, selects the requested JSON/code range with VS Code API calls, reveals it in the editor, and writes a readback receipt proving the active editor selection matched the requested range. Capability-gated on an open trusted VS Code workspace with the debugger bridge extension.

claims.proves: run.sh open --bridge requests a VS Code bridge reveal action, and the bridge uses VS Code editor APIs to set and read back the exact selected range when the live bridge is available; absent bridge/workspace fails closed instead of claiming selection
claims.does_not_prove: that the human looked at the highlighted range, or semantic correctness of the selected JSON field

cases.name: live-selected-json-field-range
cases.description: Select the stderr JSON key in a real editor via the VS Code bridge and read back SELECTED from the bridge status. Capability-gated: BLOCKED without DEBUGGER_VSCODE_WORKSPACE + active bridge.

stdout_contains: SELECTED report.json:3:26-3:34 -- VS Code API selection active; frontmost

cases.name: right-monitor-half-vertical-frontmost
cases.description: Select the stderr JSON key, raise VS Code frontmost, and place it on the right monitor at half horizontal width and full vertical height.

stdout_contains: SELECTED report.json:3:26-3:34 -- VS Code API selection active; frontmost; geometry 3840,0 1920x2160

cases.name: missing-bridge-fails-closed
cases.description: With a workspace that is not open in VS Code, bridge selection must fail closed with BRIDGE_BLOCKED rather than falling back to a fake selection claim.
command:
set -uo pipefail; WS="$(mktemp -d)"; printf '{"readiness":"READY"}
' > "$WS/report.json"; ../run.sh open "$WS/report.json" --json-field readiness --bridge --workspace "$WS" --wait-seconds 1
